claims.claim: ⚠️ **Even relatively low doses of a TCA can kill**: cardiac instability (arrhythmias, reduced contractility) and neurological instability (CNS depression, seizures).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Narrow therapeutic window; single-tablet fatalities have been reported; patients can deteriorate quickly.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Care is largely supportive**, though **sodium bicarbonate alkalinisation may be required.** **There is no antidote.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **TCAs covered:** amitriptyline, imipramine, nortriptyline, doxepin, dothiepin, clomipramine.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Signs usually appear within an hour and most within 6 hours**, but anticholinergic slowing of gut transit can make absorption unpredictable.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess:** any symptomatic patient · every deliberate self-poisoning · patients without symptoms who have cardiac or neurological disease. ⚠️ **Refer any child who took over 5 mg/kg to hospital.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Over 10–15 mg/kg: intubate, ventilate and give charcoal.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Co-ingested serotonin reuptake inhibitors** may raise TCA levels and precipitate serotonin syndrome.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sodium-channel blockade:** hypotension and reduced contractility, **a wide QRS that predisposes to VT and VF**, prolonged QT. **Reuptake inhibition:** CNS depression/coma, seizures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Anticholinergic:** sinus tachycardia · blurred vision · vomiting · delirium · ataxia · ileus · urinary retention. **Antiadrenergic:** vasodilation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **ECG on admission, repeated if abnormal: QRS over 100 ms is associated with seizures; QRS over 160 ms with ventricular arrhythmias.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **TCA levels help only if the diagnosis is in doubt — they don't predict outcome.** Also: paracetamol level, glucose if GCS reduced, blood gas for acidosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider early intubation if GCS is reduced.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Charcoal is generally contraindicated (aspiration risk)** — except over 10–15 mg/kg, when it is given **after intubation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Widened QRS or ventricular arrhythmia: sodium bicarbonate 2 mmol/kg bolus**, repeated as needed, with consideration of intubation and hyperventilation **to a pH of 7.5.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Seizures: benzodiazepines.** ⚠️ **Avoid phenytoin** — it also blocks sodium channels.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cardiac monitoring and regular ECGs.** ⚠️ **Contact ICU for altered conscious state, GCS under 12, seizures, widened QRS or arrhythmia.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Asymptomatic: investigate as above, observe 6 hours, and discharge if the ECG stays normal.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for:** all adolescents with intentional overdose · symptomatic patients · overdose with cardiovascular or neurological disease · co-ingestion of cardio-depressant drugs or MAO inhibitors. **Intentional overdose needs mental health review.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer to a tertiary centre** if there is any cardiovascular instability, or significant CNS depression/seizures. **PIPER: 1300 137 650.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge criteria:** normal GCS · normal ECG · 6 hours' observation if stable · after deliberate ingestion, a risk assessment finding a low risk of further self-harm.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) Poisoning' (Last updated June 2017), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Tricyclic_Antidepressant_(TCA)_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
